note: rk init (M1.2) stamps every `stamped` entry: for entries with a non-null `template`, the file templates/<template> is read, every {{RK_SLOT_...}} is substituted, and the result is written byte-identical to `path`. Entries with template=null are directories created empty. Unfilled slots are detected by grepping the stamped tree for `unfilled_slot_grep`; a match means a slot was missed. Layout is PRD.md:79-85 exactly: no report/ tree, no LEARNINGS.md, no SHARD_CATALOG.md, no argument/INDEX.md or DAG.md mirrors, no repo-root INDEX.md (those are prior-tool residue or M2.4/M2.6 generated outputs, not stamped structure). There are exactly THREE additions to that layout, all content rather than structure (PRD.md:79-85 fixes the DIRECTORIES): argument/thm-north-star.md, the single registry result whose contract is already known at stamp time (it is `rk init`'s own argument), seeded so PRD C2's critical-path provenance guarantee has a resolvable root from day one instead of an empty path it reports as satisfied (generality audit 2026-07-25, finding M3); runs/probe-channel.sh, the sanctioned probe-execution channel section 4b I.3 of the stamped constitution REQUIRES, without which every campaign hand-rolls the one channel its own ledger depends on (rk-z93m); and refs/manifest/SOURCES.md, the empty reference registry `rk refs add`/`adopt` append rows to (rk-tyl6). The two MACHINE artifacts beside it, refs/manifest/{checksums.sha256,sources.lock.json}, are deliberately NOT stamped: their absence is a signal the gates read (src/gates/defs.ts WARNs 'manifest absent: cannot verify cited hashes'; readLockFacts reports nothing is hash-pinned), and an empty stamped file would silence it while nothing is in fact pinned. `rk refs add`/`adopt` create them on first use. Any file stamped directly under runs/ must also be named in src/gates/runs.ts's SANCTIONED_RUNS_INFRASTRUCTURE, or the runs gate reports it as a stray file — test/templates/templates.test.ts binds the two lists.

classifications.rewritten-whole: re-stamped whole by a future `rk upgrade`; campaign-owned slot VALUES inside must be preserved by hand.
classifications.generated: a build output; never hand-edited, never stamped as authored content.
classifications.campaign-seed: stamped ONCE as a starting point, campaign-owned thereafter — `rk upgrade` never rewrites it. Distinct from authored-append-only, which is stamped as an empty skeleton and grows by appending; a seed is stamped WITH content the campaign then rewrites in place.

changelog_note: One entry per template_version, NEWEST FIRST. `rk upgrade` prints every entry strictly newer than the repo's own .rk/template-version. This exists because the interesting part of a bump is often invisible to the per-file diff `rk upgrade` otherwise prints: a brand-new stamped path does not exist in the old repo to diff against, and a new .rk/config.json key is not a stamped file at all. Each `changes` string must be self-contained and say what to DO.

changes: NEW STAMPED FILE runs/probe-channel.sh — the sanctioned, ledgered probe-execution channel section 4b I.3 has REQUIRED since 1.7.0 but that no rk command ever produced. It runs one probe script inside a run bundle, bounded by `timeout` and pinned single-threaded, refuses to overwrite an existing output.txt (results are immutable; a re-run gets a NEW bundle directory), and appends one hash-bound JSONL entry — bundle path, script sha256, output sha256, command, exit, seconds — to runs/probe-ledger.jsonl. The file does not exist in a pre-1.8.0 repo, so no diff shows it: copy it from templates/runs/probe-channel.sh.tmpl (classification campaign-seed — `rk upgrade` will never stamp or rewrite it for you), then run it with `bash runs/probe-channel.sh <bundle-dir> <script> [timeout-s]` or `chmod +x` it first. If you already stood up your own channel, the only thing you must change is its NAME and the ledger's: see the next entry.

THE CHANNEL'S RESERVATION RULES, which a hand-rolled channel almost certainly gets wrong (codex review 2026-08-14, findings P1/P2-5/P2-6 against the first cut of this same file). (1) The LEDGER, not the filesystem, decides what has already run: a bundle that appears in runs/probe-ledger.jsonl is refused (exit 4) even if its output.txt was deleted, so a cited bundle path always resolves to exactly one immutable row. (2) ONE exclusive flock on runs/ (file descriptor 9, never `flock -c` with an interpolated command string) is held across the reservation check, the run, the hashing AND the append — two concurrent launches of the same new bundle used to both pass a non-atomic `[ ! -e output.txt ]` test, both truncate output.txt and both append a competing row. Probes therefore serialize campaign-wide; a waiter blocks at most RK_PROBE_LOCK_WAIT seconds (default: this run's timeout + 60) and then fails with exit 5. (3) script_sha256 is taken BEFORE launch and re-checked after: a probe whose bytes changed while it ran gets NO ledger row at all, a runs/<bundle>/POISONED.txt naming both digests, and exit 6 — a post-run digest binds output.txt to a program that may not have produced it. (4) Bundle and script names are VALIDATED, not escaped: both must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$ with no '..' component, and the timeout must be a positive integer, else exit 2. A `"` in a filename used to append a permanently malformed line to the append-only ledger, and a `'` used to break the shell string the append ran through; escaping instead would mean requiring a JSON serializer, which this zero-dependency script will not do. TO ADOPT IN A CAMPAIGN THAT ALREADY COPIED AN EARLIER CUT OF THIS FILE (campaign-seed: `rk upgrade` will not do it for you): re-copy it from templates/runs/probe-channel.sh.tmpl and keep only your own interpreter-dispatch and determinism edits. Check your existing ledger first — `python3 -c "import json;[json.loads(l) for l in open('runs/probe-ledger.jsonl')]"` — because a malformed line already written is permanent, and duplicate `bundle` values mean some shard cites an ambiguous run.

NEW STAMPED FILE refs/manifest/SOURCES.md — the reference registry, stamped as an empty table with its ROLE/UPDATE-POLICY header and the never-fabricate-a-hash policy, so a campaign has the catalogue before its first source rather than after. It did not exist in a pre-1.8.0 repo and no diff shows it; you do not need to copy it, because `rk refs add` and `rk refs adopt` now both seed exactly this document when it is absent or blank (before 1.8.0, `rk refs add` instead threw ENOENT — after it had already written checksums.sha256 and sources.lock.json, leaving the payload pinned by both machine artifacts with no manifest row, which had to be repaired by hand-seeding SOURCES.md and re-running). The two machine artifacts refs/manifest/{checksums.sha256,sources.lock.json} are deliberately NOT stamped: `rk check` reads their ABSENCE as 'no hashes to verify / nothing pinned', and an empty stamped file would silence that truthfully-empty state. Both are created on the first `rk refs add`/`adopt`.

BEHAVIOR CHANGE in `rk check`'s runs gate: the two names runs/probe-channel.sh and runs/probe-ledger.jsonl are now sanctioned infrastructure at the top of runs/ and draw no finding, and the gate's coverage line names whichever of them is present. Every other loose file directly under runs/ is still a stray (WARN), and matching is EXACT — probe-ledger.jsonl.bak, probe-ledger-2.jsonl, and a probe-channel.sh one directory down all still warn. A campaign that stood up its own channel under different names (the constitution required the channel but never named it, so several did) will keep seeing those WARNs: rename the two files to exactly these names, and adjust the ledger path inside the channel script. Root cause: a real campaign built the channel the constitution demands and rk check reported the constitution's own mandatory artifact as loose junk in runs/.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md section 4b I.3 AMENDED (still within 1.8.0 — the review repair above landed in the same unreleased version, so this is a same-version correction, not a new bump) to describe the hardened channel's exit codes and the reservation rule the previous two changelog entries already documented but the constitution prose never caught up to: a campaign agent hitting exit 4 had no constitution text explaining what it meant. The prose now lists all six exit codes (2 validation, 3 output exists, 4 already ledgered, 5 channel busy, 6 poisoned) and states plainly that the ledger, not the filesystem, decides 'already run'. Also documented: `rk init` has no per-file mode concept, so the stamped script is not executable — invoke it as `bash runs/probe-channel.sh ...` (already the documented form) or `chmod +x` it yourself. A manifest mode field to make `rk init` stamp it executable was considered and DECLINED as scope creep for this fix; a single documented invocation covers the gap without a new stamping concept. TO ADOPT: if your CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md predates this entry, re-read section 4b I.3 directly — a diff of prose already flagged BEHAVIOR CHANGE / RESERVATION RULES above will not show this addition as new, since those entries describe the SCRIPT, not the constitution text about it.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md gain four new sections between § 4 and § 5: '4a. Predict-before-attempt and the reward ledger', '4b. Boundary-probe protocol (I.1-I.3)', '4c. Briefs and hostile verification', '4d. Worker lifecycle'. No diff of an existing constitution shows these as anything but new text — read them directly. Root cause: a real campaign ran a full research window with its reward ledger at exactly zero (closes=0, reduces=0, prunes=0 against six banked results) because the stamped constitution never described the reward protocol at all, and separately, every other proven campaign convention (boundary probes, brief format, hostile verification seats, worker-lifecycle rules) had only ever been hand-ported per campaign — and hand-porting already failed once, which is how the reward-ledger gap happened in the first place. TO ADOPT IN AN EXISTING CAMPAIGN: append the four sections to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md by hand (rewritten-whole means `rk upgrade` will not do this for you); then run `rk reward sync --dry-run` to see what the registry's ground truth implies for the ledger you never populated, and apply it if the output is sane.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md § 5's 'Recording an independent verification' subsection is REORDERED: the shard's `provenance:` frontmatter line must now be declared BEFORE `rk reward attest` runs, not after. `rk reward attest` itself changed to enforce this (it refuses to hash or write until the declaration already exists), because the declaration line is part of the bytes the record binds — writing the record first and declaring it second made the record stale on arrival. `--out` is also now confined to the reserved '.rk/provenance-<name>.json' namespace. A pre-1.7.0 constitution's text describes the OLD, now-wrong order and will walk a researcher into a command that refuses; rewrite that subsection from this version's text, do not just patch the example command.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md section 5 gains a subsection, 'Recording an independent verification (before a proved-mod-audit close can bank)'. Read it directly; no diff of an existing constitution shows it as anything but new text. Gate 8 Check 4b requires a proved-mod-audit close to be backed by a record written by someone other than the claim's prover, and the only routes are `rk verify --live`'s L5 verdict store or a JSON provenance record under `.rk/`. Campaign A ran seven windows of real cross-vendor hostile verification, recorded every event as prose under docs/worker-output/, and drew 12 [reward-tier-unbacked] structural errors the day the check landed — the constitution had never mentioned the record, and until template_version 1.6.0 no rk subcommand wrote one.

NEW COMMAND `rk reward attest --claim <id> --author <seam> --role verifier|reviewer --reason <text>` writes that record (schemas/provenance-record.v1.json). TO ADOPT IN AN EXISTING CAMPAIGN: for every proved-mod-audit close already in `.rk/reward-ledger.jsonl`, you need the verifying worker's identity seam `family|backend|model|sessionId` — read it off that worker's own transcript header (a `codex exec` log prints `model:`, `provider:`, `session id:`). If you did not keep the transcripts, the seam is NOT recoverable and must not be guessed: record a dated waiver in the campaign repo naming the affected closes instead, and start capturing worker output to a file from the next dispatch on. The record also pins the shard's sha256 at attestation time, so a shard revised after its endorsement needs a re-attest against the final bytes.

The same subsection states the three placement/timing constraints an error message alone cannot teach: the record lives DIRECTLY under `.rk/` (one level, no subdirectory — the snapshot text boundary rk check reads), a prose report is a `--source` citation and never the record itself, and the author seam must be captured while the worker's transcript is open.

NEW STAMPED FILE .gitignore — ignores build/ (generality audit 2026-07-25, finding m6/rk-zva). PRD section 3 left build/'s committed-vs-ignored status 'per config' with no config key ever built to drive it and no file stamped either way, so a first commit swept in generated site output by accident. rk's explicit default is IGNORED, because `rk render` regenerates build/site/index.html byte-for-byte and `rk check`'s freshness gate proves that every run — committing a mechanically reproducible file doubles the source of truth for nothing. A pre-1.5.0 repo has no .gitignore from rk (only bd's own, dolt-files-only one, if bd init ran) — create one by hand from templates/.gitignore.tmpl, or just add a `build/` line, if you want this default; campaign-seed means `rk upgrade` will never stamp or touch it for you once you have one.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md section 4 gets one new paragraph: the two-vendor precondition of promotion (rk-id1 part c). L5's cross-vendor rule already required this; the constitution now says so at setup time, naming the config key (`workers.assignments.verifier.hard.backend`) and the L5-soft-tier alternative for a single-vendor roster, WITHOUT stamping any vendor choice — every value that key could hold names one, and a general tool does not choose it for a stranger's campaign. No diff of an existing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md shows this paragraph as anything but new text in the middle of section 4; read it directly.

NEW STAMPED FILE argument/thm-north-star.md — the campaign's north-star contract as a real registry shard (kind: theorem, status: conjecture, no deps). No diff of your existing files shows this: the file does not exist in a pre-1.4.0 repo.

NEW .rk/config.json KEY northStarId = "thm-north-star". .rk/config.json is not a stamped template, so no diff reveals this one either. Until it is set, rk check's critical-path provenance check — every node on the path to the north star must carry cross-vendor, non-batch validation provenance — walks an EMPTY path and reports itself satisfied while covering nothing. To adopt: if you already have a registry shard for your target result, just add "northStarId": "<that id>" to .rk/config.json and stamp nothing. Otherwise create argument/thm-north-star.md per argument/README.md's frontmatter contract, with your north-star statement as its one-line `contract:`, then set the key. A northStarId that resolves to no shard is a hard ERROR, not a silent pass — so set both or neither.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md section 5 rewritten: it now names every shipped command (rk check, phase, graph, render, refs, verify, doctor, upgrade) and documents the .rk/config.json keys the gates and drivers actually read, northStarId and workers included. The 1.3.0 text hedged rk render as a command that 'may not exist yet' and never mentioned rk verify, rk graph, rk refs or rk doctor at all.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md L1 now points at `rk refs add` / `rk refs quote` for ground-truth provenance. The 1.3.0 text told the researcher to recompute hashes and grep quotes by hand — work the binary already does.

CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rule 4 and CONVENTIONS.md 'Naming and ids' corrected: registry and definition ids carry NO campaign-wide prefix (def-<slug>; lem-/thm-/prop-/cor-/op-/obs-<slug>; each equal to its filename stem). shardsPrefix is the SHARD-ID namespace for LaTeX report shards only. The 1.3.0 text told you to prefix registry ids with it, contradicting both stamped schema READMEs and every gate that reads them. NOTE: CONVENTIONS.md is authored-append-only, so upgrade will never fix it for you — rewrite that section by hand, and check whether any id you already created carries the prefix.
